title: Station2Radar: Query‑Conditioned Gaussian Splatting for Precipitation Field
claim: Conventional interpolation from sparse point measurements oversmooths structure; learned, query-conditioned placement recovers sharp fields close to the dense ground truth.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right: input, baseline, ours, ground truth; red dashed labels
description: Four square map panels sit side by side, each showing the same region with a coastline and many hollow circles for weather station locations. Panel (a), Weather Station, shows only sparse colored dots, mostly clustered at the lower right, as the raw input. Panel (b), Multiquadric Interpolation, adds smooth, blobby rainfall patches in green, yellow and red. A red dashed box labeled 'Empirical weighting' and red dashed arrows between stations mark the interpolation's behavior. Panel (c), QCGS (Ours), is bolded. It has a red dashed box labeled 'Learnable weighting' and a few overlaid ellipses showing Gaussians. It produces sharp, fragmented rainfall structures. Panel (d), Radar (GT), shows the detailed ground-truth rainfall. The eye goes first to the colorful rain regions and the red boxes, then compares (c) with (d).
caption: Construction of precipitation fields from (a) sparse AWS observations. (b) Empirical kernel-based interpolation oversmooths and blurs rainfall boundaries. (c) QCGS leverages satellite context and gauge anchors to selectively place Gaussians, producing resolution-flexible and structurally consistent fields. (d) Ground-truth radar at 2 km resolution for reference.
abstract: Precipitation forecasting relies on heterogeneous data. Weather radar is accurate, but coverage is geographically limited and costly to maintain. Weather stations provide accurate but sparse point measurements, while satellites offer dense, high-resolution coverage without direct rainfall retrieval. To overcome these limitations, we propose Query-Conditioned Gaussian Splatting (QCGS), the first framework to fuse automatic weather station (AWS) observations with satellite imagery for generating precipitation fields. Unlike conventional 2D Gaussian splatting, which renders the entire image plane, QCGS selectively renders only queried precipitation regions, avoiding unnecessary computation in non-precipitating areas while preserving sharp precipitation structures. The framework combines a radar point proposal network that identifies rainfall-support locations with an implicit neural representation (INR) network that predicts Gaussian parameters for each point. QCGS enables efficient, resolution-flexible precipitation field generation in real time. Through extensive evaluation with benchmark precipitation products, QCGS demonstrates over 50\% improvement in RMSE compared to conventional gridded precipitation products, and consistently maintains high performance across multiple spatiotemporal scales.
